sources_considered.why: Summarizes the WSJ report of the delay and the reasons behind it.
Quotes the WSJ on executives' frustration over the failure to make progress on Behemoth.
Meta's own statement on Behemoth's performance and status. This is counterevidence.
Relays a later NYT report that the release was delayed due to poor internal performance. Used as context only, because it was published after the period.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Meta reportedly delayed its Behemoth AI model rollout', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: Meta has reportedly delayed the rollout of its flagship AI model after engineers struggled to substantially improve its capabilities.

evidence_items.explanation: Two days before the post, the WSJ reported that Behemoth was delayed because engineers could not substantially improve its capabilities. This fits the reading that it was not working as intended.

evidence_items.publisher: Sherwood News (quoting The Wall Street Journal)
evidence_items.locator: quoted WSJ passage, middle of article

receipt.public_excerpt: Senior executives at the company are frustrated at the performance of the team that built the Llama 4 models and blame them for the failure to make progress on Behemoth

evidence_items.explanation: According to the WSJ, Meta executives themselves described a 'failure to make progress on Behemoth' in the period just before the post.

receipt.public_excerpt: Llama 4 Behemoth outperforms GPT-4.5, Claude Sonnet 3.7, and Gemini 2.0 Pro on several STEM benchmarks. Llama 4 Behemoth is still training

evidence_items.explanation: Meta said Behemoth beat rival models on some STEM benchmarks and was used to train its smaller models. In a narrow sense, that means it worked. But Meta also said it was still training and not released.

evidence_items.publisher: Slashdot (relaying Investing.com and The New York Times)

receipt.public_excerpt: Meta had completed training its Behemoth model by feeding in data to improve it, but delayed its release due to poor internal performance.

evidence_items.explanation: A later NYT report backs the WSJ account: the release was held back over poor internal performance, and Meta's new lab discussed dropping the model. This is context only, because it was published after the period.

unresolved_gaps: The WSJ and NYT reports rely on unnamed sources. Meta declined to comment and published no internal evaluation of Behemoth.
The WSJ article itself is paywalled. Its content is cited through Fortune and Sherwood.
